title: Drawn from the Water: The Nile to Mount Nebo
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: The Nile, among the flags: the basket of bulrushes
stops.campa: Pharaoh has decreed every Hebrew son cast into the river. A daughter of Levi hides her boy three months, then daubs an ark of bulrushes with slime and pitch and lays it among the reeds at the river's brink. His sister stands afar to watch. Pharaoh's daughter comes down to bathe; she sees the ark, hears the child weep, and has compassion. "This is one of the Hebrews' children," she says. The sister runs and fetches the child's own mother to nurse him for wages. The river that was to drown him carries him instead into the palace.
stops.quote: And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
suggested_refs: Poussin, The Finding of Moses (Louvre)
Dura-Europos synagogue fresco of the infant Moses

stops.name: The court of Pharaoh at Pi-Ramesses (Qantir)
stops.campa: Grown in the house of Pharaoh's daughter, Moses is a prince of Egypt, learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, yet the milk of a Hebrew mother is in him. The aggadah tells how as a child he took the crown from Pharaoh's head, and an angel guided his hand to a coal, so that ever after his speech was slow and his tongue heavy. He walks the granite halls of the delta capital of Rameses, a Levite disguised as an heir, and the burden of his people begins to weigh on him.
suggested_refs: colossi and pillared halls of Pi-Ramesses at Qantir
Rembrandt, Moses (unfinished)
sources: Acts 7:22 (learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians)

stops.name: Goshen: the Egyptian slain
stops.campa: Moses goes out to his brethren and looks on their burdens. He sees an Egyptian smiting a Hebrew, one of his own. He looks this way and that, and seeing no man, he strikes the Egyptian down and hides him in the sand. The next day he finds two Hebrews striving, and reproves the wrongdoer, who answers: "Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me?" So the deed is known. Pharaoh hears, and seeks to slay Moses. The prince becomes a fugitive.
stops.quote: Who made thee a prince and a judge over us? intendest thou to kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian?
suggested_refs: William Blake, Moses Slaying the Egyptian
the land of Goshen, the Israelite settlement of the eastern delta

stops.name: The well of Midian at Al-Bad' (Madyan)
stops.campa: Moses flees eastward, out of Egypt, over the wilderness to the land of Midian, and sits down by a well. The seven daughters of the priest of Midian come to draw water and fill the troughs for their father's flock, but the shepherds drive them away. Moses stands up and helps them, and waters their flock. Their father Reuel, called Jethro, marvels they are come so soon. "An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds," they say. He calls the stranger in to bread.
stops.quote: And when the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
suggested_refs: the Well of Moses at Al-Bad', Tabuk
Rosso Fiorentino, Moses Defending the Daughters of Jethro

stops.name: Midian, the house of Jethro; Zipporah
stops.campa: Moses is content to dwell with the man, who gives him Zipporah his daughter to wife. She bears a son, and he calls him Gershom, for he says, "I have been a stranger in a strange land." Forty years the prince becomes a shepherd, keeping the flock of Jethro the priest, learning the desert and its silences. In Egypt the king who sought his life dies; the children of Israel sigh under their bondage, and their cry comes up unto God. God remembers His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
stops.quote: I have been a stranger in a strange land.
suggested_refs: the oasis of Al-Bad' in Wadi Ifal
Caves of Shu'ayb (Jethro), Tabuk

stops.name: Horeb, the burning bush
stops.campa: Leading the flock to the backside of the desert, Moses comes to Horeb, the mountain of God. The angel of the LORD appears in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush; the bush burns and is not consumed. He turns aside to see this great sight, and God calls to him out of the bush: "Moses, Moses." "Here am I." "Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground." And He declares Himself the God of the fathers, come down to deliver Israel. Moses hides his face, afraid to look upon God.
stops.quote: Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.
suggested_refs: the Chapel of the Burning Bush, St Catherine's Monastery
Byzantine mosaic of the Burning Bush, Sinai

stops.name: Horeb: I AM THAT I AM, the rod and the leprous hand
stops.campa: Moses asks the Name. God answers: "I AM THAT I AM," and bids him say to Israel, I AM hath sent me. To arm his mouth against unbelief, God gives him signs. The rod cast down becomes a serpent, and Moses flees from it; taken by the tail, it is a rod again. His hand thrust into his bosom comes out leprous, white as snow; put in again, it is restored. Still Moses pleads he is slow of speech; God appoints Aaron his brother to be his mouth, and sends him back to Egypt. The bush has spoken; the exile is over.
stops.quote: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.
suggested_refs: the Tetragrammaton in the burning bush iconography
Aaron's rod that budded (Numbers 17)

stops.name: The inn on the way, the bridegroom of blood
stops.campa: On the road back to Egypt, at a lodging place, the LORD meets Moses and seeks to kill him, for his son is uncircumcised. Zipporah takes a sharp stone, cuts off her son's foreskin, and casts it at Moses' feet. "Surely a bloody husband art thou to me." So the LORD lets him go. It is a dark and terrible mercy on the threshold of the mission: the deliverer must himself be marked with the covenant of Abraham before he can carry it to Pharaoh.
stops.quote: Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.
suggested_refs: flint circumcision knives of the Bronze Age Levant

stops.name: The court of Pharaoh: let my people go
stops.campa: Aaron meets Moses at the mount of God and kisses him; together they gather the elders of Israel, and Aaron does the signs, and the people believe and bow their heads. Then Moses and Aaron stand before Pharaoh: "Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go." Pharaoh answers, "Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice? I know not the LORD." He lays heavier labour on them, straw no longer given, bricks still demanded. Aaron casts down his rod; it becomes a serpent and swallows the rods of the magicians. Pharaoh's heart is hardened.
stops.quote: Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.
suggested_refs: wall reliefs of Ramesses II enthroned
the contest of the rods before Pharaoh

segments.name: The Ten Plagues and the Passover

stops.name: The Nile turned to blood: the first plague
stops.campa: Moses meets Pharaoh at the water's brink in the morning and lifts the rod. All the waters of the Nile turn to blood; the fish die, the river stinks, and Egypt cannot drink. Seven days the blood endures. So begin the wonders in the land of Ham. The magicians ape the sign with their enchantments, and Pharaoh's heart stays hard; he turns and goes into his house, and sets not his heart to this also. The god-river of Egypt bleeds, and its people dig about the banks for water.
stops.quote: And all the waters that were in the river were turned to blood.
suggested_refs: the Nile of Egypt
medieval Haggadah illuminations of the plagues

stops.name: Frogs, lice, flies: plagues two, three, four
stops.campa: The river brings forth frogs abundantly; they cover the land, come into the houses, the bedchambers, the ovens, the kneading-troughs. Pharaoh begs relief, then hardens. Aaron smites the dust and it becomes lice in man and beast; the magicians cannot do so and confess, "This is the finger of God." Then swarms of flies fill the houses of Egypt, but in Goshen where Israel dwells there is no swarm, that Pharaoh may know the LORD is in the midst of the earth. Between plagues the king relents, and relenting, hardens again.
stops.quote: Then the magicians said unto Pharaoh, This is the finger of God.
suggested_refs: the ten plagues cycle in the Sarajevo Haggadah
the land of Goshen spared

stops.name: Murrain, boils, hail: plagues five, six, seven
stops.campa: A grievous murrain falls on the cattle of the Egyptians, and all die, but of Israel's cattle not one. Moses casts ashes of the furnace toward heaven, and boils break forth on man and beast, so the magicians cannot stand before him. Then Moses stretches the rod, and the LORD sends thunder and hail, fire running along the ground, the worst in all the land of Egypt; the hail smites herb and tree and breaks them. Only in Goshen there is no hail. Pharaoh cries, "I have sinned," and hardens once the storm is stayed.
stops.quote: The LORD sent thunder and hail, and the fire ran along upon the ground.
suggested_refs: the plague of hail in the Golden Haggadah
Bronze Age cattle burials of the delta

stops.name: Locusts and the darkness that may be felt: plagues eight and nine
stops.campa: An east wind blows all day and night, and morning brings the locusts; they cover the face of the earth, so the land is darkened, and eat every green thing the hail had left. Pharaoh confesses again, and the west wind casts them into the Red Sea. Then Moses stretches his hand toward heaven, and thick darkness covers Egypt three days, a darkness that may be felt; none rises from his place, but all the children of Israel have light in their dwellings. Nine wonders are done; the tenth is prepared.
stops.quote: And there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days.
suggested_refs: the plague of darkness in medieval Haggadot
khamsin dust-storms of Egypt

stops.name: The Passover, the blood on the lintel; the firstborn
stops.campa: The LORD sets a new beginning: this month shall be the first of months. Each house takes a lamb without blemish, kills it at even on the fourteenth, strikes the blood on the two side posts and the upper door post, and eats it roast with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, loins girt, staff in hand, in haste. At midnight the LORD smites all the firstborn of Egypt, from Pharaoh's heir to the captive in the dungeon and the firstling of beasts. Where the blood is seen, the destroyer passes over. A great cry rises in Egypt; there is not a house where there is not one dead.
stops.quote: And when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you.
suggested_refs: the seder plate and the Passover Haggadah
the blood-marked lintel in Passover art

stops.name: Rameses, the going out; six hundred thousand on foot
stops.campa: That night Pharaoh rises and summons Moses: "Get you forth, and be gone." The Egyptians press them to depart, and lade them with silver and gold and raiment, spoiling Egypt. The children of Israel journey from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot beside children, and a mixed multitude with them, and their dough unleavened, for they were thrust out and could not tarry. Four hundred and thirty years to the day, the hosts of the LORD go out of the land of bondage. Moses carries the bones of Joseph, as Joseph had sworn the children of Israel.
stops.quote: And the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot that were men, beside children.
suggested_refs: the bones of Joseph carried out of Egypt
David Roberts, The Israelites Leaving Egypt

stops.name: Succoth, the pillar of cloud and fire
stops.campa: God leads them not by the near way through the land of the Philistines, lest war turn them back to Egypt, but about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea. And the LORD goes before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, that they may go by day and night; the pillar departs not from before the people. At Succoth, the booths, the ordered march begins, harnessed and rank on rank, out of the house of servitude toward the sea.
stops.quote: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light.
suggested_refs: the pillar of cloud and fire in Exodus iconography

stops.name: Pi-hahiroth by the sea, the host of Pharaoh in pursuit
stops.campa: At God's word they turn and encamp by the sea, before Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. Pharaoh's heart hardens once more; he makes ready his chariot and takes six hundred chosen chariots and all the chariots of Egypt, and overtakes them by the sea. Israel lifts up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians march after them, and they are sore afraid and cry out. Moses answers: "Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD." The pillar of cloud moves behind them, darkness to Egypt, light to Israel, and the two camps come not near all night.
stops.quote: Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD, which he will shew to you to day.
suggested_refs: the pursuit of Pharaoh in the Golden Haggadah

stops.name: The Red Sea parted: Pharaoh's host drowned
stops.campa: Moses stretches his hand over the sea, and the LORD drives it back by a strong east wind all night, and makes the sea dry land; the waters are divided. Israel goes into the midst of the sea on dry ground, the waters a wall on their right and on their left. The Egyptians pursue into the midst, and the LORD troubles their host, and takes off their chariot wheels. In the morning watch Moses stretches his hand again; the sea returns in its strength, and the waters cover the chariots and horsemen; there remains not so much as one of them. Israel sees the Egyptians dead upon the shore.
stops.quote: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.
suggested_refs: the crossing of the Red Sea, Dura-Europos synagogue
the drowning of Pharaoh in the Nuremberg Chronicle

stops.name: The shore of the sea, the Song of Moses and Miriam
stops.campa: On the far shore Moses and the children of Israel sing this song unto the LORD: "I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea." They sing of the right hand made glorious in power, of the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea, of the LORD who shall reign for ever. Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, takes a timbrel, and all the women go out after her with timbrels and dances, and she answers them: "Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously."
stops.quote: I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.
suggested_refs: the Song of the Sea in the Torah scroll's brick-pattern layout
Miriam with the timbrel, medieval manuscript

stops.name: Marah, the bitter water sweetened
stops.campa: Three days they go into the wilderness of Shur and find no water. They come to Marah, but cannot drink its waters, for they are bitter; therefore the name is called Marah, bitterness. The people murmur against Moses: "What shall we drink?" He cries to the LORD, who shows him a tree; he casts it into the waters, and the waters are made sweet. There God makes for them a statute and an ordinance, and proves them, saying: if thou wilt hearken to the voice of the LORD, and do that which is right, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, for I am the LORD that healeth thee.
stops.quote: I am the LORD that healeth thee.
suggested_refs: the springs of 'Ain Hawarah
the tree cast into the bitter waters

stops.name: Elim, twelve wells and threescore and ten palms
stops.campa: They come to Elim, where are twelve wells of water and threescore and ten palm trees, and they encamp there by the waters. Twelve springs for the twelve tribes, seventy palms for the seventy elders, says the tradition, reading the oasis as a sign. After the bitterness of Marah, God gives them abundance and shade; the wandering people rest a while in a green place at the desert's edge, the Gulf shining below, before the long ascent into the wilderness of Sin and the mountain of God.
stops.quote: And they came to Elim, where were twelve wells of water, and threescore and ten palm trees: and they encamped there by the waters.
suggested_refs: the palm oasis of Wadi Gharandel

stops.name: The wilderness of Sin, the manna and the quails
stops.campa: In the wilderness of Sin the whole congregation murmurs for the flesh-pots of Egypt. At even quails come up and cover the camp, and in the morning, when the dew is gone, upon the face of the wilderness lies a small round thing, small as the hoar frost. "It is manna," they say. What is it? Bread the LORD has given them to eat. It is like coriander seed, white, tasting of wafers made with honey. They gather it every morning, an omer a man; on the sixth day, double, for the seventh is the sabbath, and none is found. Forty years this bread of heaven does not fail.
stops.quote: This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.
suggested_refs: the gathering of manna, Bury St Edmunds Bible
the golden pot of manna kept in the ark

stops.name: Rephidim, the water from the rock at Horeb
stops.campa: At Rephidim there is no water, and the people chide with Moses and are almost ready to stone him: "Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?" The LORD tells Moses to go on before the people, take the rod that smote the river, and stand upon the rock in Horeb: "thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it." Moses smites the rock before the elders, and water gushes out, and the people drink. He calls the place Massah and Meribah, temptation and strife, because they tempted the LORD.
stops.quote: Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock in Horeb; and thou shalt smite the rock, and there shall come water out of it.
suggested_refs: the Rock of Horeb at Wadi Feiran
Tintoretto, Moses Drawing Water from the Rock

stops.name: Rephidim, the battle with Amalek; the upheld hands
stops.campa: Amalek comes and fights with Israel in Rephidim. Moses sends Joshua to choose men and go out to war, and himself stands on the top of the hill with the rod of God in his hand. When he holds up his hand, Israel prevails; when he lets it down, Amalek prevails. His hands grow heavy; so Aaron and Hur put a stone under him, and stay up his hands, the one on the one side, the other on the other, and his hands are steady until the going down of the sun. Joshua discomfits Amalek with the edge of the sword. The LORD swears war with Amalek from generation to generation.
stops.quote: And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Israel prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.
suggested_refs: John Everett Millais, Victory O Lord! (the upheld hands)
the altar Jehovah-nissi

stops.name: Rephidim, Jethro's counsel; the seventy judges
stops.campa: Jethro the priest of Midian comes to Moses in the wilderness, bringing Zipporah and her two sons whom Moses had sent back. Moses tells him all the LORD has done to Pharaoh, and Jethro rejoices and blesses the LORD. He sees Moses judging the people alone from morning to evening and warns him he will surely wear away: "The thing that thou doest is not good." He counsels rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, tens, to bear the small matters, that Moses bear only the great. Moses hearkens; the burden is shared. Then Jethro departs into his own land.
stops.quote: The thing that thou doest is not good. Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee.
suggested_refs: the appointment of the seventy elders

stops.name: Sinai, the theophany; the thunder and the trumpet
stops.campa: In the third month they come to the wilderness of Sinai and camp before the mount. God calls Moses up and offers the covenant: if Israel obey, they shall be a peculiar treasure, a kingdom of priests, an holy nation. The people are sanctified two days, their garments washed, bounds set about the mount. On the third morning there are thunders and lightnings, a thick cloud, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud, so all the people tremble. Mount Sinai is altogether on smoke, for the LORD descends in fire; the whole mount quakes greatly, and the trumpet sounds long and louder. Moses speaks, and God answers by a voice.
stops.quote: And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire.
suggested_refs: the summit of Jebel Musa (Mount Sinai)
the giving of the Law, Sarajevo Haggadah

stops.name: Sinai, the Ten Words spoken
stops.campa: Out of the fire and cloud God speaks all these words, the Ten, in the hearing of all the people: I am the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me. No graven image; the Name not in vain; the sabbath kept holy; father and mother honoured; not to kill, nor commit adultery, nor steal, nor bear false witness, nor covet. The people see the thunderings and remove and stand afar off, and say to Moses, "Speak thou with us; but let not God speak with us, lest we die."
stops.quote: I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
suggested_refs: the two tablets of the Decalogue in synagogue art
Rembrandt, Moses with the Tablets of the Law

stops.name: Sinai, forty days in the cloud; the pattern of the Tabernacle
stops.campa: Moses draws near to the thick darkness where God is, and the elders behold the God of Israel, under His feet as it were a paved work of a sapphire stone. Moses goes up into the mount, and a cloud covers it; the glory of the LORD abides upon Sinai, and to Israel below the appearance is like devouring fire on the top of the mount. Moses enters the cloud and is in the mount forty days and forty nights, while God shows him the pattern of the Tabernacle, the ark, the mercy seat, the lampstand, and gives him the two tables of testimony, written with the finger of God.
stops.quote: And Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights.
suggested_refs: the Tabernacle plan in printed Hebrew Bibles
the ark of the covenant and the mercy seat

stops.name: Sinai, the golden calf; the tablets shattered
stops.campa: Below, the people gather to Aaron: "Make us gods, which shall go before us; for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him." He takes their golden earrings, fashions a molten calf, and they say, "These be thy gods, O Israel," and rise up to play. On the mount God tells Moses to go down, for the people have corrupted themselves. Moses descends with the two tables; he sees the calf and the dancing, and his anger waxes hot, and he casts the tables from his hands and breaks them beneath the mount. He burns the calf, grinds it to powder, strews it on the water, and makes them drink.
stops.quote: And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.
suggested_refs: Poussin, The Adoration of the Golden Calf
the breaking of the tablets in Haggadah art

stops.name: Sinai, the plague of the calf; the sons of Levi
stops.campa: Moses stands in the gate of the camp: "Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me." All the sons of Levi gather to him, and at his word go through the camp, and there fall about three thousand men. The LORD plagues the people for the calf. Moses goes up again and pleads: "Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written." He asks to see God's glory, and is hidden in a cleft of the rock while the glory passes, beholding the back parts, for no man sees God's face and lives.
stops.quote: Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.
suggested_refs: the cleft of the rock at Sinai
the thirteen attributes of mercy proclaimed

stops.name: Sinai, the second tables; the shining face
stops.campa: Moses hews two tables of stone like the first and goes up again forty days and forty nights, eating no bread, drinking no water. The LORD passes before him and proclaims His name: merciful and gracious, longsuffering, forgiving iniquity, and He writes again the words of the covenant, the ten commandments. Moses comes down from the mount with the two tables, and knows not that the skin of his face shines from talking with God. Aaron and the people are afraid to come nigh him; so he puts a veil upon his face, and takes it off when he goes in to speak with the LORD.
stops.quote: The skin of his face shone while he talked with him.
suggested_refs: Michelangelo, Moses (San Pietro in Vincoli), the horns of light
the veiled face of Moses

stops.name: Sinai: the Tabernacle raised; the glory fills it
stops.campa: The willing-hearted bring their offerings, and Bezaleel and Aholiab, filled with the spirit of God in wisdom, make all the work: the boards of shittim wood, the curtains of blue and purple and scarlet, the ark, the table, the golden candlestick, the altars, the laver, the priestly garments and the breastplate of twelve stones. On the first day of the first month of the second year, Moses rears up the Tabernacle. Then a cloud covers the tent, and the glory of the LORD fills it, so that Moses cannot enter. By day the cloud is on the tent, by night fire, in the sight of all Israel throughout their journeys.
stops.quote: Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
suggested_refs: the Tabernacle and its court in scholarly reconstructions
the breastplate of the high priest (the Urim and Thummim)

stops.name: Taberah and Kibroth-hattaavah, the fire and the graves of lust
stops.campa: The people complain, and the fire of the LORD burns among them and consumes the uttermost parts of the camp; Moses prays, and the fire sinks. They call the place Taberah, burning. Then the mixed multitude lusts for flesh and weeps for the fish and cucumbers of Egypt, loathing the manna. The LORD takes of the spirit on Moses and puts it on seventy elders, who prophesy; Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp. A wind brings quails from the sea, but while the flesh is yet between their teeth a plague smites the greedy, and they bury them at Kibroth-hattaavah, the graves of lust.
stops.quote: Would God that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!
suggested_refs: the seventy elders receiving the spirit
the quails brought by the wind

stops.name: Hazeroth, Miriam's leprosy and Moses' meekness
stops.campa: At Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman he had married, saying, "Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us?" And the LORD hears. Now the man Moses is very meek, above all the men upon the earth. The LORD calls the three out, comes down in the pillar of cloud, and declares that with Moses He speaks mouth to mouth, not in dark speeches. His anger kindles; Miriam becomes leprous, white as snow. Moses cries, "Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee," and after seven days shut out, she is received again.
stops.quote: With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the LORD shall he behold.
suggested_refs: the oasis of 'Ain Khadra (Hazeroth)

stops.name: Kadesh-barnea, the twelve spies and the fainthearted report
stops.campa: From Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran Moses sends twelve men, a prince of every tribe, to spy out Canaan. Forty days they search it, and return bearing a cluster of grapes on a staff between two, and pomegranates and figs. It flows with milk and honey, they say, but the people are strong, the cities walled, and there are giants, the sons of Anak; "we were in our own sight as grasshoppers." The congregation weeps all night and murmurs to return to Egypt. Only Caleb and Joshua rend their clothes and say the land is good and the LORD is with them. The people would stone them.
stops.quote: And there we saw the giants... and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.
suggested_refs: the spies bearing the cluster of Eshcol (the Israel tourism emblem)
Tell el-Qudeirat (Kadesh-barnea)

stops.name: Kadesh, the sentence of forty years
stops.campa: The glory of the LORD appears in the tent; He would smite the people with pestilence, but Moses pleads His name and mercy among the nations, and God pardons yet decrees the sentence: none of the men who saw His glory and His miracles in Egypt and tempted Him these ten times shall see the land; their carcases shall fall in the wilderness. Forty years, a year for each day the spies searched the land, until all that generation die, save Caleb and Joshua. The ten evil spies die of the plague. Presuming to go up in the morning, the people are smitten by the Amalekites and Canaanites down to Hormah.
stops.quote: After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years.
suggested_refs: the wilderness of Paran and Zin

stops.name: The wilderness, Korah swallowed by the earth
stops.campa: Korah of the Levites, with Dathan and Abiram and two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, rises against Moses and Aaron: "ye take too much upon you." Moses bids each bring his censer, and let the LORD show whom He has chosen. He warns the congregation to depart from the tents of these wicked men. As he ends speaking, the ground cleaves asunder; the earth opens her mouth and swallows Korah's men and their houses and their goods, and they go down alive into the pit. Fire from the LORD consumes the two hundred and fifty who offered incense; their censers are beaten into plates for the altar.
stops.quote: And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods.
suggested_refs: Botticelli, The Punishment of Korah (Sistine Chapel)
Aaron's rod that budded, kept before the testimony

stops.name: Kadesh (Meribah), the striking of the rock; the sin that bars him
stops.campa: In the fortieth year the people come again to Kadesh, and there is no water, and they chide with Moses, wishing they had died with their brethren. God tells Moses to take the rod and speak to the rock before their eyes, that it give forth water. But Moses gathers them and cries, "Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?" and smites the rock twice with the rod. Water comes out abundantly, and the congregation drinks. Yet because he believed not, to sanctify God before Israel, the LORD says he shall not bring this congregation into the land. It is the waters of Meribah, strife.
stops.quote: Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.
suggested_refs: the waters of Meribah-Kadesh
Rembrandt school, Moses Striking the Rock

stops.name: Mount Hor, the death of Aaron
stops.campa: Miriam dies at Kadesh and is buried there. Then, on the edge of Edom, at Mount Hor, the LORD tells Moses that Aaron shall be gathered to his people, for he too rebelled at Meribah. Before all the congregation Moses brings Aaron and his son Eleazar up the mount, and strips Aaron of his priestly garments and puts them upon Eleazar; and Aaron dies there on the top of the mount. Moses and Eleazar come down, and when all the congregation see that Aaron is dead, they mourn for him thirty days, all the house of Israel. The office passes; the brother is gone.
stops.quote: And Aaron shall be gathered unto his people: for he shall not enter into the land which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah.
suggested_refs: Jebel Harun (Mount Aaron) above Petra
the shrine of Aaron on Mount Hor

stops.name: The way of the Red Sea, the fiery serpents and the bronze serpent
stops.campa: Compassing the land of Edom, the soul of the people is much discouraged, and they speak against God and Moses: "there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread." The LORD sends fiery serpents among them, and much people of Israel die. They repent and come to Moses, who prays for them. The LORD says, Make thee a fiery serpent and set it upon a pole; every one that is bitten shall look upon it and live. So Moses makes a serpent of brass and sets it on a pole; and if a serpent bites any man, he looks and lives.
stops.quote: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
suggested_refs: the Nehushtan, the serpent of brass on the pole
the copper-mines of Punon (Feinan)

stops.name: Beer, the Song of the Well
stops.campa: Passing the brooks of Arnon and the border of the Amorites, Israel comes to Beer, the well; that is the well whereof the LORD spake to Moses, Gather the people, and I will give them water. Then Israel sings this song, a joy after so much murmuring: "Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it." The nobles and princes of the people dig it with the lawgiver's staff. From the wilderness they journey on to Mattanah, and Nahaliel, and Bamoth, and to the valley in the country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks toward Jeshimon.
stops.quote: Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it.
suggested_refs: the wells of the Arnon country (Wadi Mujib)

segments.name: The Plains of Moab and Nebo

stops.name: The valley of Pethor, Balaam and the speaking donkey
stops.campa: Balak king of Moab, dreading Israel encamped in his plains, sends for Balaam the seer to curse them. Balaam saddles his donkey and rides; the angel of the LORD stands in the way with a drawn sword, unseen by the prophet but seen by the beast. Three times the donkey turns aside, and Balaam smites her; then the LORD opens the donkey's mouth, and she says, "What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?" Balaam's eyes are opened; he sees the angel and falls flat. Brought to the high places, he can only bless: "How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob!"
stops.quote: And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?
suggested_refs: the Deir Alla inscription naming Balaam son of Beor
Rembrandt, Balaam and the Ass

stops.name: The plains of Moab by Jordan, the words of Deuteronomy
stops.campa: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, in the fortieth year, the eleventh month, Moses begins to declare the law. He rehearses the whole journey from Horeb, the giving of the commandments, the wandering; he pleads with the new generation to love the LORD, to keep His statutes, to choose life. He recites the great Shema: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD." He sets before them blessing and cursing, life and death, and sings his song of witness, and blesses the twelve tribes each by name, as a father over his children before he goes.
stops.quote: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: and thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
suggested_refs: the Nash Papyrus (Decalogue and Shema)
the plains of Moab above the Jordan

stops.name: Mount Nebo, the top of Pisgah: the sight of the whole Land
stops.campa: Moses goes up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. And the LORD shows him all the land: Gilead unto Dan, all Naphtali, Ephraim and Manasseh, all Judah unto the utmost sea, the south, and the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, unto Zoar. This is the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, given to their seed: he is caused to see it with his eyes, but shall not go over thither. A hundred and twenty years old, his eye not dim, his force not abated, he looks upon the promise he may not enter.
stops.quote: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.
suggested_refs: the summit of Mount Nebo (Siyagha), the Moses Memorial
the Serpentine Cross of Mount Nebo, overlooking the Jordan

stops.name: The valley over against Beth-peor: no man knoweth his sepulchre
stops.campa: So Moses the servant of the LORD dies there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD. The aggadah tells it was by the kiss of God, His breath drawing forth the soul of the faithful shepherd. And God Himself buries him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth-peor; but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day. The children of Israel weep for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days. There arises not a prophet since in Israel like unto Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face. Joshua takes up the mantle; the people go over Jordan without him.
stops.quote: And he buried him in a valley in the land of Moab, over against Beth-peor: but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day.
suggested_refs: Ayoun Musa (the Springs of Moses) below Nebo
the tradition of the death by the kiss of God (Bava Batra 17a)
sources: Talmud Bava Batra 17a; Sotah 13b (God buries Moses)
